searchText: 1) Isn't prysm utilising `getPayloadBodies` Engine API requests to deduplicate transaction and withdrawal data already? I'm a little bit lost here, withdrawals from the payload are irrelevant for block processing: once you have validated the payload on sync, you know that the withdrawals agree with the ones that you can get from the beacon state. You can save the payload and you do not need that payload again to process the beacon state: you get the withdrawals from it and you know the corresponding payload did honor those withdrawals. This is not the case for the requests, that are external inputs to state transition that are coming from the block. Perhaps we should add this to the agenda today. excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: I'm a little bit lost here, withdrawals from the payload are irrelevant for block processing: once you have validated the payload on sync, you know that the withdrawals agree with the ones that you can get from the beacon state. You can save the payload and you do not need that payload again to process the beacon state: you get the withdrawals from it and you know the corresponding payload did honor those withdrawals. This is not the case for the requests, that are external inputs to state transition that are coming from the block. Perhaps we should add this to the agenda today. If it's not on the issue I'll add it now

excerpts.author: g11tech
excerpts.content: my take on 7702 complexity:

excerpts.author: g11tech
excerpts.content: https://x.com/Gajpower/status/1816528691985572090

excerpts.author: lightclient
excerpts.content: this is an application concern, not the protocol

excerpts.author: g11tech
excerpts.content: we are making it easy for application to fckup

excerpts.author: lightclient
excerpts.content: it's already easy with proxies, which we added specifically in eip-7

excerpts.author: g11tech
excerpts.content: its also an attack vector where you might get a user to write something via contract A which when delegated to contract B might mean something drastically different

excerpts.author: lightclient
excerpts.content: yes we've discussed this issue at great length. this is why persistence of the delegation is good, it allows other wallets to actually see that they are delegated to a different smart contract wallet.

excerpts.author: g11tech
excerpts.content: why persist storage, thats the main issue, persitance of delegation without storage won't be an issue

excerpts.author: lightclient
excerpts.content: because smart contract wallets w/o storage aren't very useful - you want to write to storage delegate keys with more strict access policies. additionally, smart contract wallets would need to be completely rewritten to be stateless which we are hoping to avoid by going with 7702

excerpts.author: g11tech
excerpts.content:
you dont need to use EOA storage and EOA can have/seek this data from other contracts without worrying about some other contract coming in and modifying storage,

so essentially what you said is possible even without EOA having its own storage

excerpts.author: g11tech
excerpts.content: and with 7702 it can do multiple contract interactions to get the data it needs

excerpts.author: lightclient
excerpts.content: yep and we have also looked into this already. not only are the costs higher and requires writing smart contract wallets differently, it doesn't work well with verkle because in the future you will want to use the storage in your account header as it will be much cheaper than bringing in additional leaves

excerpts.author: g11tech
excerpts.content:
> verkle because in the future you will want to use the storage in your account header as it will be much cheaper than bringing in additional leaves

you mean accessing different branches, leaves would anyway be there in both cases

excerpts.author: lightclient
excerpts.content: whatever the terminology is, you'll need to bring another account into the witness

excerpts.author: g11tech
excerpts.content: but only if the storage accessed is in the account header branch

excerpts.author: g11tech
excerpts.content: else if you access another branch which most likely you would, there might not be substantial cost saving

excerpts.author: lightclient
excerpts.content: you would probably not access another branch, smart contract wallets don't need much storage

excerpts.author: g11tech
excerpts.content: ok, i don't think savings if there are any are worth the risk, but yea just my personal opinion 🙂

excerpts.author: g11tech
excerpts.content:
actually there is one thing we can do:

EOA subaccounts, which are basically hash(eoa,address) which is where the storage for that particular delegation gets written

excerpts.author: g11tech
excerpts.content: should make things cleaner overall as well and we can also have persisted storage

excerpts.author: lightclient
excerpts.content: yep vitalik also proposed this idea (although he proposed eoa addr + 1 for storage). i think it's a massive hack and doesn't fix the fact that smart contract wallets today face the same issue
